Topic1.Title: Opening, Announcements, and Agenda Amendment
Topic1.Summary: Mayor Brockett opened the meeting with an announcement that the 2026 boards and commissions recruitment period is closed and interviews are underway, with appointments set for the March 5 meeting. Council conducted roll call and approved a motion to swap agenda items 2A and 3 so that open comment would precede the Black History Month declaration.

Topic2.Title: Open Comment
Topic2.Summary: Residents spoke on South Boulder Recreation Center, with many urging the city to keep its pool, gym, and core amenities and to avoid cutting services. Other speakers addressed South Boulder outdoor tennis courts, the 15-minute neighborhood concept, the Home Act housing bill, Excel Energy power outages and resilience hubs, and towing practices. Speakers also raised concerns about Valmont coal ash remediation, homeless sweeps, and city budget priorities, including the cost of administrative buildings. Council members and staff responded briefly, with staff clarifying that no decision to close South Boulder Rec Center has been made.

Topic3.Title: Black History Month Declaration
Topic3.Summary: Council Member Adams read a declaration recognizing February 2026 as Black History Month, highlighting the theme of a century of Black history commemorations and local Boulder history. The declaration encourages community members to learn about Black history, support Black-owned businesses, and work toward racial healing. Representatives of the Black Women's Alliance at CU Boulder received the declaration and spoke about their work.

Topic4.Title: Consent Agenda
Topic4.Summary: Council considered consent agenda items 4A through 4C, which had no discussion or requests for removal. A motion and second were made, and the consent agenda was approved unanimously by roll call vote.

Topic5.Title: Call-Up Check-In
Topic5.Summary: Council reviewed two landmark alteration certificates in Mapleton Hill Historic District: demolition and rebuild of an accessory building at 2408 street, and a new primary building at 2439 Broadway. No council member requested to call either item up for further review, so both proceeded without discussion.

Topic6.Title: Public Hearing: 550 Arapahoe Avenue Rezoning Ordinances
Topic6.Summary: Council held second readings of Ordinances 8736 and 8737 to rezone about 2.65 acres at 5501 and 5505 Arapahoe Avenue from BC1 to MU4, along with adjacent rights-of-way. Staff explained the rezoning supports redevelopment under the East Boulder form-based code and aligns with the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan's Mixed-Use Transit Oriented Development designation. The applicant presented the project's transit, bike, and mobility features, and one public speaker opposed the density increase. Council discussed the project's architecture and the irony that the desired mixed-use zoning required a separate rezoning, then unanimously adopted both ordinances.

Topic7.Title: 2026 Policy Statement on Regional, State, and Federal Issues
Topic7.Summary: Intergovernmental Affairs Officer Heather Staer presented staff recommendations for updates to the 2026 policy statement, based on the IGA committee's January 22 review. Proposed additions include human rights language, support for federally funded research and labs, housing and workforce housing language, construction defects reform, coal ash mitigation, wildfire guidance, data center water and energy conservation, and orphaned well cleanup. Council members discussed the data center water and energy language, with staff noting local water providers would be involved in any determinations. Council members generally supported the recommended updates and some noted existing policies already covering electrification and distributed generation.

Topic8.Title: State Bill HB26-1010 (Home Act) Position Discussion
Topic8.Summary: Staff presented HB26-1010, which would allow qualifying nonprofits, schools, churches, and other entities to pursue residential development on sites five acres or less through an administrative approval process in any zone. Staff outlined benefits, including potential affordable housing development, and drawbacks, including preemption of home rule, limits on local standards, and a broad nonprofit definition. Council members asked detailed questions about height, architecture, affordability, transit access, and local planning, and expressed concerns about lack of guardrails. The council decided by straw poll to take an amend position and requested amendments limiting the bill to urban areas, tightening the nonprofit definition, applying zone height standards, requiring a demonstrated housing need, and ensuring consistency with the comprehensive plan.

Topic9.Title: Council Retreat Follow-Up
Topic9.Summary: Assistant City Manager Matt Chzanski presented staff's scoping of council's retreat priorities, including bicycle security and theft reduction, wildfire home hardening and assessment, a tip credit ordinance exploration, power resiliency, and sister city program updates. Council reviewed process improvements, including board packet timing, CAC request tracking, historic landmark presentation streamlining, and a request to avoid meetings past 10 p.m. Council members requested clarification on Title 9 status, ebike regulation research, and timing for the June tip credit ordinance. Staff committed to sending revised project language and following up on food systems, public safety updates, agriculture, and parking questions.

Topic10.Title: Closing Remarks and Adjournment
Topic10.Summary: Council Member Tara raised concerns about downtown parking rates and asked staff to review parking trends following a previously approved fee increase. Council Member Adams requested updates on the ENCAR property, and staff committed to providing information as it is compiled. Mayor Brockett then adjourned the meeting at 9:11 p.m.
